experiment: Dilution/re-isolation retention of receptor-regulated CheA kinase activity (32P-ATP, phospho-CheY SDS-PAGE assay) in ex vivo Tsr–CheA–CheW complexes
buffer: 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, pH 7.5 (challenge); activity buffer 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 10% glycerol, 0.5 mM EDTA, 160 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2 and 0.5 mM PMSF (assay)
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr receptor in isolated membranes plus CheW (assembled complex)
construct_or_mutation: Tsr-ex vivo complex: wild-type full-length E. coli Tsr, CheA and CheW co-expressed in E. coli RP3098; complex isolated in membranes by sonication (entry is the 134-residue CheA N-terminal fragment, so this is full-length CheA)
other_conditions: 100-fold dilution, up to 23 hours; repeated dilution/re-isolation cycles tested; Tsr-ex vivo CheA:receptor approx. 1:8 to 1:4; CheA is a 134-residue-entry protein but full-length used; high-salt isolation buffer contained sodium phosphate but assays were in Tris
dynamics_type: CheA association with assembled receptor lattice; no detectable dissociation on hour timescale (slow/ultrastable binding)
author_claim: Once assembled in live cells, the signaling complex retains CheA activity for at least 23 hours after 100-fold dilution, indicating a dissociation half-life of days or longer.
anchor: Thus, the assembled signaling complex is ultrastable, with a half-life of days or longer regardless of whether assembly occurs in live cells
locator: Results, 'Assembled signaling complexes are ultrastable in vitro' (Fig. 2B,C); conditions: Methods and Fig. 2 legend
caveat_note: Readout is retention of kinase activity only (CheA protein was not directly quantitated for this lower-density complex). Absence of loss shows no dissociation on the hours window, not absence of faster local motions. Paper notes the discrepancy with a 12-minute FRAP exchange half-life in live cells at 20 °C and proposes an unidentified disassembly machinery lost on isolation; this is not resolved by the data.

experiment: Equilibrium exchange assay: preformed ex vivo complexes challenged with 50 µM kinase-dead CheA mutant, kinase activity monitored over time
buffer: 50 mM Tris, pH 7.5-HCl, 160 mM NaCl, and 5 mM MgCl2
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr receptor, CheW; excess kinase-dead CheA
construct_or_mutation: Tsr-ex vivo complex with wild-type E. coli CheA; challenger kinase-inactive CheA H68Q/G470K (written H48Q/G470K in Methods subheading and Fig. 4 legend)
other_conditions: 50 µM challenger, about 100-fold excess over active CheA (0.5 µM); no pelleting before challenge; same results reported if complexes were pelleted first (data not shown)
dynamics_type: CheA subunit exchange between complex and free pool (not detected)
author_claim: Preformed complexes show little or no exchange of bound CheA with free CheA, so bound CheA dissociates extremely slowly.
anchor: It follows that preformed complexes exhibit little or no exchange of their bound CheA with free CheA under near-physiological buffer conditions at 22° C.
locator: Results, 'Ultrastability prevents exchange with free CheA or CheW' (Fig. 4B); conditions: Methods and Fig. 4 legend
caveat_note: Exchange is inferred from unchanged kinase activity, assuming an exchanged inactive CheA would reduce activity. The same inactive mutant competes when present during assembly, supporting that the assay detects incorporation. Mutant is numbered H68Q in text and H48Q in figure legend/Methods heading; the inconsistency is unresolved. In contrast to the 12-minute FRAP half-life in live cells (cited), the authors suggest a cellular disassembly system; alternative intrinsic membrane properties cannot be excluded.

experiment: Dilution/re-isolation retention of CheA protein (CheA:Tsr by SDS-PAGE) and attractant-dependent kinase activity in Tsr-IM in vitro complexes
buffer: 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, pH 7.5 (challenge); activity buffer 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 10% glycerol, 0.5 mM EDTA, 160 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2 and 0.5 mM PMSF (assay)
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr in inner membranes, CheW, with or without serine
construct_or_mutation: N-terminal 6-His S. typhimurium CheA and CheW with E. coli Tsr (Tsr-IM in vitro complex); S. typhimurium CheA, not E. coli CheA
other_conditions: 100-fold dilution, up to 23 hours; CheA per receptor 1:9 to 1:5; Tris buffer in assays
dynamics_type: CheA association with assembled receptor lattice; no detectable dissociation over 23 h
author_claim: The Tsr-IM in vitro complex retains CheA protein, CheW and receptor-regulated kinase activity for 23 hours after 100-fold dilution.
anchor: yielding (i) no measurable loss of CheA protein ( Fig. 2A ) (ii) no detectable loss of attractant-dependent, receptor-regulated, CheA kinase activity
locator: Results, 'Assembled signaling complexes are ultrastable in vitro' (Fig. 2A); conditions: Fig. 2 legend and Methods
caveat_note: CheA is the S. typhimurium protein with a His tag, so this is homolog evidence for the E. coli target. The authors note trans-species composition may subtly perturb the system. No dissociation on hours timescale does not exclude faster motions.

locator: Results, 'Ultrastability prevents exchange with free CheA or CheW' (Fig. 4A,B); conditions: Methods

experiment: Time-dependent loss of CheA from Tsr-IM complexes assembled without CheW, after 100-fold dilution (SDS-PAGE/Coomassie)
buffer: activity buffer 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 10% glycerol, 0.5 mM EDTA, 160 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2 and 0.5 mM PMSF
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr in inner membranes, no CheW (binary Tsr–CheA complex)
construct_or_mutation: 6-His S. typhimurium CheA with E. coli Tsr, CheW omitted
other_conditions: CheA:receptor ratio significantly lower than with CheW; times given only in Fig. 3
dynamics_type: fast CheA dissociation from binary receptor–CheA complex (minutes)
author_claim: Without CheW the binary complex dissociates within minutes, so ultrastability requires all three core proteins.
anchor: The resulting binary complex dissociates within minutes of dilution, leading to rapid loss of CheA from the membranes
locator: Results, 'Assembled signaling complexes are ultrastable in vitro' (Fig. 3, left panel)
caveat_note: No rate constant is reported; 'within minutes' is qualitative. S. typhimurium CheA used. Control for pelleting artefacts: CheA freely dissociates when CheW is absent.

experiment: Challenge of preformed Tsr-IM in vitro complexes with low ionic strength, pH and temperature; CheA:Tsr ratio and kinase activity after re-isolation
buffer: standard 160 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, pH 7.5; challenge buffers with varied salt or pH at 20 mM NaCl
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr in inner membranes, CheW; NaCl, KCl, MgCl2 etc. as shielding ions
construct_or_mutation: 6-His S. typhimurium CheA and CheW with E. coli Tsr (Tsr-IM in vitro); also Tar-SM and Tsr-ex vivo for activity
other_conditions: 45 min incubation, 100-fold dilution; 100 mM NaCl rescued stability; low pH 5.0 rescued while pH 8.6 gave additional destabilization; 4 °C stable, 40 °C unstable, above 35 °C partial inactivation
dynamics_type: electrostatically driven CheA dissociation from lattice under non-physiological conditions
author_claim: Low ionic strength or high pH dissociates the complex through electrostatic repulsion among acidic components, whereas physiological conditions give ultrastability.
anchor: We found that exposure of the preformed complexes to a low ionic strength was highly destabilizing.
locator: Results, 'Ultrastability can be disrupted by electrostatic repulsion' (Fig. 6A-C); conditions: Fig. 6 legend
caveat_note: Electrostatic explanation is inferred from salt and pH dependence and APBS isopotential contours, not measured directly. S. typhimurium CheA used. Loss of activity at high pH or temperature can reflect inactivation, not only dissociation.

experiment: Long-term half-life measurement: retention of receptor-stimulated CheA kinase activity of Tsr-IM in vitro complexes after 100-fold dilution (three independent time courses)
buffer: activity buffer 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 10% glycerol, 0.5 mM EDTA, 160 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2 and 0.5 mM PMSF
ligand_or_partner: E. coli Tsr in inner membranes, CheW
construct_or_mutation: 6-His S. typhimurium CheA and CheW with E. coli Tsr (Tsr-IM in vitro)
other_conditions: stable for first 24 hours; inactivation onset between 36 and about 100 hours; inactivation then takes 12 to 24 hours
timescale: t1/2 (longest activity half-life observed) = approximately 125 hours (5.2 days) (three independent time courses, onset 1.5 to 4 days)
author_claim: The complex has an activity half-life of days, up to about 5.2 days.
anchor: Overall, the longest half-life of activity observed thus far is approximately 125 hours
caveat_note: Loss of kinase activity may reflect CheA dissociation, denaturation or proteolytic degradation; the paper states these cannot be distinguished. The onset time is variable and the value is a longest observed, not a fitted rate constant. S. typhimurium CheA used.
